messages:
jordan: Heads up — CI started failing on the macOS/arm and manylinux wheels after merging the tokenizers bump. Safety scan flagged CVE-2026-XXXX in tokenizers' wheel build.
maya: saw the CI logs. failing step is `pip install tokenizers==0.12.7` — error is `unsupported wheel abi` on older runners.
sam: Do we know if this is an upstream wheel issue or our constraints? Could be a new manylinux tag they published.
evan: quick grep: the wheel claims manylinux_2_24_x86_64 but contains symbols that trigger pip to choose a different binary. There's also a report on GH about a corrupted metadata file in the 0.12.7 release.
chloe: dependabot opened a PR upgrading tokenizers and transformers. dependabot: PR #492: bump tokenizers 0.12.6 -> 0.12.7 (includes patch for CVE-2026-XXXX)
jordan: I think priority is twofold: 1) triage CVE for severity + exploitability, 2) get CI green (temporary patch), 3) plan backport for our pinned releases.
maya: For CI hotfix we can pin tokenizers to 0.12.6 in the constraints file and pin the poetry.lock resolution via `poetry lock --no-update` on the CI image, or add a `--no-binary=tokenizers` fallback.
sam: prefer constraints file approach: add a constraints.txt in repo with `tokenizers==0.12.6` and modify CI pip install to `pip install -r requirements.txt -c constraints.txt`. That avoids mutating poetry.lock in PRs.
evan: downside: poetry users won't pick up constraints unless we ensure the build uses pip for the wheel install step. Our test matrix currently mixes poetry and pip in different jobs.
chloe: Alternative: regenerate poetry.lock from a clean env with poetry 1.6 and commit the lockfile, then run full test matrix. That may be heavier but cleaner.
jordan: CVE detail: it's a high severity local privilege escalation vector during wheel build for C extensions; upstream labels it fixed but the release artifacts are suspect.
maya: Action plan proposal: A) add CI constraint pin for tokenizers to stop regressions (hotfix) B) open internal rollback PR for tokenizers in prod images C) request upstream to reupload signed wheels or provide source distribution for reproducible build D) schedule a backport branch where we pin tokenizers to a patched 0.12.x and bump transformers compat if needed.
sam: I'll draft the CI change. Suggested patch:
```
# .github/workflows/python-tests.yml
- run: pip install -r test-requirements.txt -c ci/constraints.txt
```
and ci/constraints.txt contains `tokenizers==0.12.6`

evan: I'll take the upstream contact and ask for signed wheel reupload + sha256. Also start a quick local rebuild of their sdist to validate the fix.
chloe: If upstream can't reupload quickly, we should publish an internal wheel to our private artifact repo with the patched build and update CI to prefer our index: `pip install --index-url https://artifacts.redwood.example/simple tokenizers==0.12.6`.
jordan: Good. Also audit logs: we should capture the time range of when the bad wheel was first pulled in by our build infra (check build artifacts registry and deployagents). Put an incident tag in our tracking system if we see any production deploys with the vulnerable wheel.
maya: I'll open an ENG-SEC ticket with triage notes, attach CI links and a minimal repro for the corrupted wheel.
sam: PR incoming in ~20m with constraint change and docs note. @chloe please coordinate internal artifact if needed.
evan: marking this as P0 for now until the pinned constraint lands and we confirm no prod deploys used the faulty wheel.
chloe: ack. Will update the ticket and ping infra for any images built in last 48h.
jordan: thanks team — keep updates brief here. :thumbsup:
